newsitem.title: USA: Cablevision buying N.Y. area systems from TCI.
newsitem.headline: Cablevision buying N.Y. area systems from TCI.

text.p: Cablevision Systems Corp. said Monday it will buy 10 cable television systems in the New York area from Tele-Communications Inc., the nation's biggest cable company, for more than $500 million in stock.

The agreement will bring Cablevision's total number of New York-area customers to 2.5 million from 1.7 million, the companies said, and give TCI a 33 percent stake in Cablevision, which will continue to be controlled by the family of Cablevision Chief Executive Officer James Dolan.
"It's a good deal all the way around, a win-win," said industry analyst Chris Dixon at PaineWebber.
"It's a phenomenal deal for both companies," said money manager Mario Gabelli, whose funds owned about 3.8 million Cablevision Class A shares at the end of March.
Investors registered their approval by driving Cablevision's Class A stock up $10.375 to $45 on the American Stock Exchange while TCI rose $1 to $16.06 on Nasdaq.
The Cablevision stock, worth about $422 million at Friday's closing prices, was worth nearly $550 million based on Monday's market price.

The deal will fill holes in Cablevision's New York-area operation and help it invest in telecommunications and programming services, analysts said. It plans to have 100 channels on its New York area cable systems in the next two years and will also move to higher-speed data transmission.

Under the deal, Cablevision, the sixth-largest cable operator in the United States, will give TCI 12.2 million shares of Cablevision Class A stock and assume about $669 million of TCI debt associated with the systems, located in New Jersey, Long Island and New York's Rockland and Westchester counties.
TCI will also get two seats on Cablevision's board.
The 820,000 customers in the 10 systems fit well into the operations of Cablevision, which is based in Woodbury, N.Y., and has systems in 19 states, analysts said.

While Cablevision is taking on debt in the transaction, the systems it is acquiring generate more than $200 million in cash flow, which will help it service its debt load, the companies said. Cash flow measures earnings before taxes, interest, depreciation and other items.
The deal will also lessen TCI's massive debt load of about $15 billion, which company officials have cited as a key goal.
TCI, based outside Denver, said it expected to make similar deals with other cable companies in a bid to cut its sprawling cable systems down to a more manageable size.
The Dolan family will retain control of Cablevision since it owns all Class B stock, which has more voting power. Charles Dolan is chairman and his son James is chief executive.
